messages:
maria: heads up — our sample-app starter broke on Bun and Deno after the recent package.json changes. it works fine in node (esm) but installers choke.

maria: error seen when installing with bun: 
```
$ bun install
error: Could not resolve package entry "./dist/index.cjs" from 'redwood'
```

josh: ugh. which field did we change? exports/main/module?

maria: we added a conditional exports map for ESM/CJS per the new rollout: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

sam: bun and deno treat exports differently — bun prefers the package's "type" and may not follow conditional entries the same as node. also deno uses import maps or esm-only entrypoints.

maria: sample-app did `import Redwood from 'redwood'` and then runtime "Cannot find module" on bun. node resolves to mjs fine.

kat: could be the package's "type": "module" plus providing cjs target confuses bun. what's package.json top-level?

maria: top-level has "type": "module" now (we moved to ESM-first). we kept cjs build for compatibility.

josh: short-term fix: add a flat fallback entry in exports that points to an ESM file at the top-level for non-node resolvers. e.g. add "default": "./dist/index.mjs" OR a legacy "main": "./dist/index.cjs". bun sometimes prefers main or module depending on version.

sam: also typings: TS consumers import types from 'redwood' and tsc can't find index.d.ts because our "types" field points at dist/types/index.d.ts but exports hides it. tsc uses package resolution differently.

maria: great call. I just tried adding "main": "./dist/index.cjs" and "module": "./dist/index.mjs" plus "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" — bun install succeeds, but deno still rejects because it doesn't do node-style resolution.

josh: for deno we should publish a separate deno-friendly bundle or mention a deno-import URL in docs. we can't aim for perfect behavior across every runtime via exports alone.

kat: follow-up: can we change the SDK packaging script to emit an additional small entrypoint file at root like redwood.cjs.js and redwood.mjs.js that just re-exports the compiled files? that gives non-conditional resolvers something to grab.

maria: I'll try that. also adding a note in the sample-app README about bun/deno quirks + recommended install commands.

build-bot: CI: build/package: succeeded for node v18 and v20, failed lint:bundler on bun v1.2.0 (seen in matrix).

sam: we should pin a test in our onboarding e2e matrix: run sample-app with bun and deno check (just basic import smoke test). catches regressions early.

josh: agree. can you open a tiny infra ticket? tag me and eng-runtime. I'll add a candidate fix for the package layout.

maria: created tracker: https://linear.app/RW/issue/RW-4579-package-entries-bun-deno-interop — added reproducer and steps. tagging @josh and @sam.

kat: once we land, also bump the sample-app dependency and add a CI job that tries `bun --version` then `bun install && bun run start` as smoke.

maria: thanks team. this was surprising for a small change — packaging is deceptively tricky across runtimes :facepalm:
